_about: Blue Fit muscle database. One entry per muscle group the app tracks (ids match MuscleGroup in src/core/types.ts). Exercise lists are not stored here: they come from the exercise library (src/core/seed/library.json, each exercise's `volume`), so the exercise database links to this file by muscle id. Evidence tags: R = research, C = coaching practice, J = our call (judgment). Sets are per week, sets that hit the muscle only partly count as half.

maxSetsPerWorkout.note: Growth levels off at about 11 sets per muscle in one workout (Remmert 2025, preprint). 12–13 is a warning (J).

twoDaysAbove.note: Same weekly sets grow the same on 1 or 2 days (Schoenfeld 2019; Pelland 2024). More than 11 a week won't fit one workout, so split it.

growthReps.note: Muscles grow about the same anywhere in this range when sets end close to failure (Schoenfeld 2017, 2021).

goals.growth: Mass gain: grow muscle. Most sets 6–30 reps, a couple short of failure, rests 90 s+.
goals.strength: Strength: lift heavier. Key lifts at 6 reps or less, rests 3 min+, fewer total sets.
goals.endurance: Endurance: last longer. Most exercises 15+ reps, rests 90 s or less.
goals.maintain: Maintain: keep what you have with less time. About a third of your growth sets, kept heavy (Bickel 2011).

muscles.name: Back
muscles.does: Pulls the arms down and back, and holds the spine straight.

angles.name: lats
angles.what: Arms pulled down from overhead, or to the hips with straight arms.

angles.name: upper back
angles.what: Rows: elbows pulled back, shoulder blades squeezed.

angles.name: lower back
angles.what: Holding the spine straight while bending at the hips.

stretch.how: Lats with the arm fully overhead: single-arm pulldown, pullover.
stretch.note: Added by analogy with the studied muscles.

heavyLight.why: Big muscle trained with compound lifts: heavy rows also build strength.

recoveryHours.note: After heavy rows or deadlifts. Lighter work: about 48 h.

failure.safe: Machine and cable pulldowns and rows.
failure.avoid: Deadlifts, barbell and dumbbell rows (form breaks first).

setup: Chest up, shoulders down before you pull.
tips: Think elbows, not hands: pull with the elbows.
Let the lats stretch fully at the top of each rep.
avoid: Swinging the body to move the weight.
Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears.

muscles.name: Chest
muscles.does: Pushes the arms forward and brings them across the body.

angles.name: upper
angles.what: Pressing or flying with the arms angled up (incline).

angles.name: mid/lower
angles.what: Flat or downward pressing, dips.

stretch.how: Deep dumbbell press or fly, cable fly with the arms wide.
stretch.note: Added by analogy with the studied muscles.

heavyLight.why: Big muscle trained with compound presses.

failure.avoid: Barbell bench press without a spotter or safeties.

setup: Shoulder blades pinched back and down on the bench.
tips: Lower slowly and get a full stretch at the bottom.
avoid: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Elbows flared straight out to the sides.

muscles.name: Front delts
muscles.does: Raises the arm forward and overhead.

angles.name: press
angles.what: Overhead and chest presses work it a lot already.

heavyLight.why: Gets plenty of work from presses; extra direct work is optional.

setup: Sit tall, back against the pad.
tips: Count chest and shoulder presses: they already train it.
avoid: Arching the lower back to finish a press.

muscles.name: Side delts
muscles.does: Raises the arm out to the side. Gives the shoulders their width.

angles.name: raise
angles.what: Arm out to the side, from the hip to shoulder height or higher.

stretch.how: Cable lateral raise starting with the hand across the body.

heavyLight.why: Small muscle, isolation work; growth is the same at any reps. Moderate to high reps are easier on the shoulder.

failure.safe: Cable and machine raises, dumbbell raises.

setup: Slight lean forward, elbow a little bent.
tips: Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
Cables keep tension at the bottom, where dumbbells go slack.
avoid: Swinging the weight up with the hips.
Going so heavy the traps take over.

muscles.name: Rear delts
muscles.does: Pulls the arm back and out. Rounds out the back of the shoulder.

angles.name: reverse fly
angles.what: Arms pulled back and out, straight-ish.

heavyLight.why: Small muscle, isolation work; growth is the same at any reps.

failure.safe: Machine and cable reverse flies, face pulls.

setup: Chest on the pad, arms straight in front.
tips: Rows with the elbows out also train it.
avoid: Squeezing the shoulder blades instead of moving the arms.

muscles.name: Traps
muscles.does: Lifts, squeezes and lowers the shoulder blades. Fills out the upper back and neck line.

angles.name: shrug
angles.what: Upper traps: shoulders straight up to the ears.

angles.name: mid/lower
angles.what: Shoulder blades squeezed back, or pulled down while the arms go overhead.

heavyLight.why: Shrugs can go heavy, but growth is the same at any reps.

failure.safe: Machine and cable shrugs, Kelso shrug on a machine.

setup: Stand tall, arms straight, grip firm (straps help).
tips: Hold the top for a second.
Rows and deadlifts also work it.
avoid: Rolling the shoulders in circles.
Bending the elbows to help.

muscles.name: Biceps
muscles.does: Bends the elbow and turns the palm up.

angles.name: long head
angles.what: Curls with the arm behind the body (stretched).

angles.name: short head
angles.what: Curls with the arm in front of the body.

angles.name: brachialis
angles.what: Under the biceps: curls with the thumb up or palm down. Pushes the biceps up.

stretch.how: Incline curl or preacher curl, all the way down.

heavyLight.why: Small muscle, isolation work; growth is the same at any reps. Lighter sets are easier on the elbows.

failure.safe: Cable and machine curls, dumbbell curls.

muscles.keyLifts: None (isolation only). Rows and pulldowns train it indirectly.
setup: Elbows still, at your sides or on the pad.
tips: Straighten the arm fully at the bottom.
Back work counts as half a set each.
avoid: Swinging the body.
Elbows drifting forward at the top.

muscles.name: Triceps
muscles.does: Straightens the elbow. Two-thirds of the upper arm.

angles.name: long head
angles.what: Arm overhead: crosses the shoulder, so it's stretched there.

angles.name: lateral head
angles.what: Pushdowns and presses with the arm at the side.

angles.name: medial head
angles.what: Works in every triceps move, most near lockout.

stretch.how: Overhead extension with the elbows high.

heavyLight.why: Growth is the same at any reps; heavy extensions are hard on the elbows.

failure.safe: Cable pushdowns and extensions, machine dips.
failure.avoid: Lying or incline barbell extensions (bar near the head).

setup: Elbows fixed, only the forearms move.
tips: Chest and shoulder presses count as half a set each.
avoid: Elbows flaring out.
Leaning over the bar to push it down.

muscles.name: Forearms
muscles.does: Grips, and bends and lifts the wrist.

angles.name: flexors
angles.what: Gripping and curling the wrist up (palm-side).

angles.name: extensors
angles.what: Lifting the back of the hand.

heavyLight.why: Small muscle; grip from pulling already trains it.

setup: Forearms on a bench, wrists just past the edge.
tips: Heavy pulling without straps trains grip.
avoid: Bouncing the weight at the bottom.

muscles.name: Quads
muscles.does: Straightens the knee. The rectus femoris also lifts the thigh at the hip.

angles.name: squat
angles.what: Knees and hips bend together: squats, leg press, lunges.

angles.name: extension
angles.what: Knee only, the hip still: the only way to grow the rectus femoris well.

stretch.how: Deep knee bend; leg extension with the seat back.
stretch.note: Pedrosa 2022; seat back study via Jeff Nippard.

heavyLight.why: Big muscle: heavy squats or presses plus lighter extensions.

recoveryHours.note: After heavy squats. Machines only: about 48 h.

failure.safe: Leg press, leg extension, Smith squat with safeties.

setup: Feet where the knees can travel forward over the toes.
tips: Feet lower on the leg press = more quads.
Lower slowly, about 3 s.
avoid: Locking the knees hard at the top.
Cutting depth as the weight goes up.

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.does: Bends the knee and straightens the hip. Crosses both joints.

angles.name: knee flexion
angles.what: Leg curls: the knee bends.

angles.name: hip hinge
angles.what: Bend forward at the hips with a straight back, then stand up.

stretch.how: Seated leg curl (hips bent) and Romanian deadlifts.
stretch.note: Maeo 2021: seated beat lying leg curls.

heavyLight.why: Big muscle: heavy hinges plus lighter curls.

recoveryHours.note: Hinges make it sore for longer. Curls only: about 48 h.

setup: Leg curl: knees just past the seat edge, pad above the heels.
tips: Train both the knee and the hip end every week.
Hips back on a hinge, not down.
avoid: Rounding the lower back on hinges.
Hips lifting off the pad on curls.

muscles.name: Glutes
muscles.does: Straightens the hip and moves the leg out to the side.

angles.name: glute max
angles.what: Hip straightening: hip thrusts, deep squats, hinges.

angles.name: glute medius
angles.what: Leg out to the side.

heavyLight.why: Big muscle trained with compound lifts.

failure.avoid: Barbell hip thrusts without a setup that lets you bail.

setup: Hip thrust: upper back on the bench, shins vertical at the top.
tips: Squats, lunges and hinges count as half a set each.
Want less glute? Stop squats at parallel.
avoid: Arching the lower back to finish the rep.

muscles.name: Adductors
muscles.does: Pulls the legs together. A big part of thigh size from the front.

angles.name: adduction
angles.what: Legs pulled together; wide squats help too.

heavyLight.why: Mostly machine work; growth is the same at any reps.

muscles.keyLifts: None (deep and wide squats train it indirectly).
setup: Start with the legs as wide as feels safe.
tips: Hold the squeeze for a second.
avoid: Letting the weight slam the legs open.

muscles.name: Calves
muscles.does: Points the foot down: pushes you up on your toes.

angles.name: straight-knee
angles.what: Standing raises: the upper calf (gastrocnemius).

angles.name: bent-knee
angles.what: Seated raises: the lower calf (soleus).

stretch.how: Full stretch at the bottom, heel down, pause there.

heavyLight.why: Heavy (6–10) and light (20–30) calf raises grew the same in a direct study.

setup: Balls of the feet on the edge, heels free.
tips: Pause 2 s at the bottom so the tendon can't bounce you up.
avoid: Short, bouncy reps.

muscles.name: Abs
muscles.does: Bends and twists the trunk, and braces it.

angles.name: rectus abs
angles.what: Curling the ribs toward the hips.

angles.name: obliques
angles.what: Twisting and side bending.

heavyLight.why: Growth is the same at any reps.

tips: Add weight like any other muscle.
avoid: Pulling on the neck.
Moving at the hips instead of curling the spine.

muscles.name: Neck

angles.name: flexion
angles.what: Chin toward the chest.

angles.name: extension
angles.what: Head back.

failure.avoid: All neck work: stop a few reps short.

tips: Shrugs train the upper neck line indirectly.
avoid: Jerking the head.
Heavy weight right away.
